_notes: official_domains are used only to tag a result as 'official' vs 'aggregator' by matching the <source url> domain Google News RSS already returns — no separate official-newsroom RSS feed is fetched, because both guessed feed URLs from the original spec (Nestle, General Mills) were verified dead (HTTP 404) before this file was written. TMICC's own newsroom (news.magnumicecream.com) was confirmed real but has no RSS/Atom feed at all.
query is the exact string sent to Google News RSS's q parameter — kept deliberately specific (full name / ticker, not bare 'Magnum') to avoid matching unrelated uses of short/generic names.
confidence on official_domains: 'confirmed' means a real page was fetched and checked this session; 'likely' means a standard corporate-domain guess not independently checked.

companies.name: The Magnum Ice Cream Company
companies.query: "The Magnum Ice Cream Company" OR TMICC
companies.query_note: bare MICC was dropped — confirmed via a live run to collide with 'Mission and Installation Contracting Command' (US Army), an unrelated acronym

_press_notes: For every existing company/topic query, fetch_competitor_news.py also runs a second, press-restricted variant appending a Google site: OR-group across every domain above (e.g. '<query> (site:ft.com OR site:bbc.com OR ...)'). Live-tested before building this: Google News RSS genuinely honors the parenthesized multi-site OR syntax — confirmed by fetching a real query and checking every returned <source> was actually one of the 3 test domains and actually about TMICC, not generic noise. Items matching one of these domains are tagged source_type='press' (a tier above 'aggregator', below nothing — it's not 'official' since none of these are TMICC/competitor-owned, but it's not generic aggregator noise either).
